name: Data Structures and Algorithms
shortDescription: Learn data structures and algorithms with small examples in JavaScript, C, C++, Python, C#, and Java. Explore lists, searching, sorting, trees, and graphs step by step.
highlights: 28 lessons with six language choices
Search, sort, explore trees and graphs
Practice questions and source download

name: Object-Oriented Programming
shortDescription: Object-oriented programming groups data and useful actions together. We will build tiny JavaScript objects for a library and see how classes help us make more than one object.
highlights: Learn about classes are plans
Learn about getters provide a value
Learn about composition builds from parts

name: Design Patterns
shortDescription: A design pattern is a reusable idea for arranging code. It is not code you must copy everywhere. We will compare small JavaScript examples and learn when each idea helps.
highlights: Learn about strategy functions
Learn about facades offer a small doorway
Learn about shared state needs care

name: System Design
shortDescription: Learn how app parts work together in 30 clear lessons. Follow requests, plan data, explore caching and scaling, and work through library, chat, short-link, feed, and upload designs.
highlights: 30 lessons with simple diagrams
Databases, scaling, and reliable requests
Five worked app designs and practice

name: Microservices
shortDescription: Microservices divide a larger application into small services with clear jobs. We will plan a library example and learn the extra costs of communication, testing and failures.
highlights: Learn about contracts explain requests
Learn about timeouts bound waiting
Learn about trace a request across parts

name: Software Testing
shortDescription: Software testing checks whether a program behaves as expected. We will use tiny examples to practise choosing inputs, checking results and explaining bugs.
highlights: Learn about boundaries catch small mistakes
Learn about make a bug report useful
Learn about accessibility is part of quality

name: Unit Testing
shortDescription: Unit tests check small pieces of code. We will practise using simple JavaScript functions and explicit checks before moving to a separate test runner.
highlights: Learn about name the rule
Learn about fresh data for each test
Learn about use several cases

name: Selenium
shortDescription: Selenium drives a browser so a test can use a page much like a person does. We will check tiny pages using Python, clear locators and explicit waits.
highlights: Learn about find several elements
Learn about check selected state
Learn about find an element again after change

name: Playwright
shortDescription: Playwright checks websites in real browsers. These lessons use tiny local page examples so you can learn locators, actions and assertions without needing an online account.
highlights: Learn about labels identify inputs
Learn about check a checkbox
Learn about isolate test state

name: Cypress
shortDescription: Cypress tests frontend behaviour in a browser. We will use a blank local practice page to learn queries, clicks, inputs and controlled network responses.
highlights: Learn about type into a field
Learn about work with checkboxes
Learn about keep tests independent

name: Jest
shortDescription: Jest runs automated JavaScript tests. We will write small tests, read their results and learn how to keep tests clear and repeatable.
highlights: Learn about check lists and text
Learn about choose a mock return value
Learn about control a timer

name: Vitest
shortDescription: Vitest runs automated JavaScript tests. We will write small tests, read their results and learn how to keep tests clear and repeatable.
highlights: Learn about partial object checks
Learn about restore a spied method
Learn about dom tests need an environment

name: Clean Code
shortDescription: Clean code is code that people can read and change with confidence. We will improve small JavaScript examples by naming things clearly, keeping jobs small and making assumptions visible.
highlights: Learn about keep one job in a function
Learn about comments explain reasons
Learn about refactor without changing behaviour

name: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
shortDescription: Cybersecurity protects information and systems from misuse and mistakes. This course teaches everyday defensive habits through fictional school examples and safe local demonstrations.
highlights: Learn about use strong unique passwords
Learn about keep software updated
Learn about back up and practise recovery
